\[
H = 1 - \frac{1}{1 + (D / D_0)^{2n}},\quad D = \sqrt{f_x^2 + f_y^2},\ D_0 = 0.1,\ n = 2
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(D\): The distance from the center of the spectrum in cycles per pixel
- \(f_x, f_y\): The frequency along x and y in cycles per pixel
- \(D_0\): The cutoff frequency
- \(n\): The order

D is the distance of a frequency from the center of the spectrum, in cycles per pixel, so the filter does the same thing on any image size. Gonzalez and Woods measure D in samples of the padded spectrum. Divide their value by the padded size to get the one here. The high-pass filter is 1 minus the Butterworth low-pass filter. Ringing near edges comes from the impulse response of H, which is wider the sharper the cutoff.
